### HTML scraping

We compared paragraph text alone with paragraphs plus page headings (H1–H6). Both models used TF-IDF word features and logistic regression on `r word_pcs` principal components. We split the `r nrow(pages)` pages retained by the starter HTML filter into training and holdout sets, keeping repeated URLs together. Both tasks used the same `r length(test_rows)` held-out pages.

Adding headings raised AUC from `r auc(task_results$auc[1])` to `r auc(task_results$auc[2])`, but accuracy at the 0.5 cutoff fell from **`r pct(task_results$accuracy[1])` to `r pct(task_results$accuracy[2])`**. Headings helped rank pages by relevance, while the paragraph-only model correctly classified more pages at the chosen cutoff.

### Bigrams

Using paragraphs and headings, we added `r bigram_pcs` components from TF-IDF bigrams to a second logistic regression that used the word model's predicted log-odds. We used out-of-fold word predictions to train this second model and compared it with a second logistic regression using only those log-odds.

Adding bigrams raised accuracy from **`r pct(task_results$accuracy[3])` to `r pct(task_results$accuracy[4])`**, a net gain of `r task_results$correct[4] - task_results$correct[3]` correctly classified pages. AUC slipped from `r auc(task_results$auc[3])` to `r auc(task_results$auc[4])`. The gain at the 0.5 cutoff was small and did not extend to how well the model ranked pages.
